adjudication_label: batch_2:Competing processes: size decrease vs. coalescence
canonical_question: Does the 'size decrease' observed at 973 K contradict the 'coalescence' that is also described as 'very active' at this temperature?

question_variants.question: Does the 'size decrease' observed at 973 K contradict the 'coalescence' that is also described as 'very active' at this temperature?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text resolves the apparent contradiction by explaining that the size decrease (due to evaporation) overlaps with the very active coalescence process at 973 K, and this size decrease is not captured in the size distribution measured after the 15-minute interval.

answers.answer: The text states: 'As this phenomenon overlaps with the coalescence that is very active at 973 K, this size decrease is not captured in the size distribution measured after 15 min at 973 K'. This indicates that the size decrease (evaporation) and coalescence happen simultaneously, and the measurement method (15 min snapshot) misses the transient size decrease.
answers.measurement_outcome: Size decrease not captured in 15 min distribution
answers.mechanism: Overlap of evaporation-induced size decrease and active coalescence
answers.boundary_limitation: Size decrease masked by coalescence in time-averaged measurements
evidence_spans: In the present work, we used in situ scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), corroborated with atomistic simulations, to study in real‐time and at the atomic scale the structural and compositional evolution of AuCoCuNiPt NPs from 298 to 973 K.
These in situ insights into the thermodynamic properties of AuCoCuNiPt HENA reveal their poor structural stability at high temperature due to atomic diffusion that cannot be considered as sluggish.
